body: A useful language model should know when to answer and when to say "I don't know." Can we improve that decision by training the model itself or by training a separate component to check its answers? We study both approaches on Qwen3-14B for factual questions, using a score that rewards correct answers, penalizes mistakes, and allows abstention. Across three training seeds and two held-out confidence thresholds, a learned answer selector improves threshold-averaged utility over the original model's calibrated confidence filter. On TriviaQA, mean coverage increases from 20.2% to 30.9%, while the pooled error rate among scored answers decreases from 23.0% to 14.5% under exact-match grading. The tested reinforcement-learning changes do not establish consistent gains. On NQ-Open, the selector improves threshold-averaged utility over the filter but still performs worse than always abstaining. A partial human-reviewed audit preserves the TriviaQA finding. Our results support learning to select answers in this setting while showing that reliable abstention across datasets remains unresolved.
summaryZh: 文章探讨了语言模型在事实问答中如何通过自我训练或引入独立验证组件来提升“拒绝回答（Abstention）”的决策能力。以Qwen3-14B为测试对象，研究表明学习型答案选择器能够提高阈值平均效用，但在部分数据集上仍无法超越无条件拒绝。研究为提高模型的可靠拒绝机制提供了实证参考。
